name: The Effects
label: Dischord
lede: Devin Ocampo, Matt Dowling and David Rich had spent years in other people's bands and finally ended up in one together. They cut nine songs with J. Robbins in Baltimore and sent them to Dischord.

eras.title: A new band, not a reunion
eras.text: Most new DC bands are old bandmates reshuffled. The Effects pitched themselves as the opposite: Ocampo, Dowling and Rich had talked about it for years, and in January 2014 all three were between bands.

years.src: Dischord: The Effects · Bandcamp Daily · Wikipedia
years.h: Three musicians between bands start the Effects
years.p: [[Devin Ocampo|10bc183b-b6a8-4769-9e7a-0637d0f8a7a8]] sings and plays guitar, Matt Dowling plays bass and keys, David Rich drums. That's how Dischord's own bio describes the lineup.
years.xp:
Ocampo brought the longest résumé: [[Smart Went Crazy|d9c78028-a30b-470b-b964-2f85cab51cc2]], [[Faraquet|e866e006-4c80-4753-b53f-1bc5d88ccddd]], [[Medications|c545a7bf-c8d7-4368-8009-22e19d8911ce]] and [[Deathfix|db0e5c06-c091-46d4-bd42-5ba2ee299123]], plus time backing [[Mary Timony|d9c8dc3c-15b8-40d5-8153-ae9214aeef55]], [[J. Robbins|3babd931-a940-43a8-b629-d7aed5b821d9]] and [[Beauty Pill|976b28a1-dd68-4c43-ba08-ba15b58963b2]], often on drums. Dowling had played bass in [[Deleted Scenes|ed530932-648a-4e28-8bba-507e02986a60]]; Rich drummed in the instrumental band Buildings. Dowling's and Rich's earlier records came out on Sockets, a local label that's now defunct.

Dischord's bio says the musicians had known each other for years, and individual projects kept getting in the way.

years.p: Self-released in 2014, it's the first thing the Effects put out.
A second self-released single in 2014. Its B-side gives the 2017 album its title, though the song isn't on the album.

eras.title: Singles, then Magpie Cage
eras.text: The Effects built their name one self-released two-song single at a time. Then they drove nine songs up to J. Robbins' Magpie Cage studio in Baltimore.

years.h: Two more singles, each with a B-side
years.p: Essentially Broken comes with The Clarity Of Open Spaces, and Fix As The Reason with Close The Gap. Both are self-released.

years.src: Dischord: The Effects · Dischord: Eyes to the Light
yt: Old Soul, live in Philadelphia, October 2016
years.h: J. Robbins of Jawbox mixes the Effects at Magpie Cage
years.p: The trio records and mixes nine songs with [[J. Robbins|3babd931-a940-43a8-b629-d7aed5b821d9]] at his Baltimore studio. Ocampo had worked with Robbins before, but this time Robbins sits behind the board.
years.xp:
Robbins fronted [[Jawbox|016fba14-1fc6-4986-86c2-2113ec9b28de]]. Ocampo had played with him before, in Robbins' own solo band among others.

The nine songs become Eyes to the Light the following year.

eras.title: Eyes to the Light
eras.text: Three years in, the Effects landed on Dischord with a debut critics filed under technical DC post-hardcore. Reviewers reached for prog, not punk, as the comparison.

years.cap: The Effects at DC9, Washington, September 2017
q: The 'we got chops' end of post-hardcore.
years.src: Dischord: Eyes to the Light · Dischord news · Bandcamp Daily · Washington City Paper · Wikipedia
yt: Anchors Aweigh, live at Comet Ping Pong, January 2018
years.h: Eyes to the Light comes out as Dischord No. 185
years.p: Nine songs on LP, CD and digital, from New Isolation to the 6:29 closer Moving On.
years.xp:
Dischord announced the album on August 9 and opened pre-orders on its own store and Bandcamp, with East Coast and Midwest dates promised for the fall.

Bandcamp Daily made it Album of the Day on October 19. Joe Gross heard "complex, almost proggy trio workouts," King Crimson in the motion, and Ocampo's voice "keening and wailing." He singled out the vocal hook on Anchors Aweigh and the chugging back half of Low Lier.

Washington City Paper's headline said the Effects put the power in power trio.

years.cap: The Effects at DC9, Washington, September 26, 2017
yt: Live at the Black Cat, October 2017
years.h: The Effects take the album to the East Coast and Midwest
years.p: Dates through the fall, including DC9 in Washington on September 26 and an October show at the Black Cat.

eras.title: Ocampo and Watt
eras.text: Dischord still lists the Effects as active, but by 2019 Ocampo was being billed elsewhere as formerly of the band. His next project put him on stage with Minutemen bassist Mike Watt.

years.h: Ocampo plays with Mike Watt at the Black Cat's 25th
years.p: Devin Ocampo, Renata Ocampo and [[Mike Watt|568203ae-c27b-4990-8997-09c0d5c0de77]] play together for the first time at the Black Cat's anniversary show in DC.

years.h: Apparatus puts Ocampo and Watt on Org Music
years.p: The single by Devin Ocampo, Renata Ocampo and Watt comes out April 13. Org Music's notes call Devin Ocampo formerly of the Effects.
